rationale: Evidence from iteration 7 (outer sensors at x = +/-0.07, all else as iteration 5) is the best raced result at 42.8697. Progress rose on both s-bend (0.0409 to 0.0424) and slalom (0.035 to 0.0374). The oval also gained progress (0.2126 to 0.2261). Line loss appeared once per run on the oval (0.6 events on average, up from 0), so the wider outer span is near the edge of usable sensing on tight bends, but it is still net positive. max_error stayed at 0.0614 to 0.0622 on every track, so the off-track limit is still exceeded. The gain and ki/kd changes in iterations 3 to 6 moved the score by under 0.5 in total. Iteration 6 showed that base_speed 1.2 cut oval progress from 0.213 to 0.124 with s-bend and slalom flat, so speed is the lever with the largest measured effect on the oval, which carries most of the score. I keep the best design's geometry (+/-0.07 outer, +/-0.03 inner, 0 centre, weights +/-1.5 / +/-0.75 / 0) and controller gains (kp 2.5, ki 0.5, kd 0.2, last_direction). I change one group: base_speed from 1.4 to 1.5. Expected result, not measured: oval progress rises above 0.226 because the trend from 1.2 to 1.4 was strongly positive, while s-bend and slalom remain near 0.042 and 0.037. Risk: higher speed may increase slip and outward drift, so max_error could exceed 0.0622 and line loss could rise on the oval. If progress falls or line_loss_events rises above 0.6, return base_speed to 1.4 (iteration 7). Measurements requested: all metrics plus noise_robustness, to see whether the oval gain comes from speed and whether max_error is sensor noise or a fixed bias.
